# EC49FOF — Actual DFS forcing horizons in the frozen signed-prefix BRC cache family

2026-11-14 · `AUTHOR_PROVED / EXACT_FINITE_VERIFIED / TWO_IMPLEMENTATIONS_ON_WITNESSES / NOT_REVIEWED`

Scientific pin: `fc0f038e7bfd12c886b4d37f900bfb770c0f61ab`. Original master input SHA256 `cd9a50799536d2b96230777b5392b1d742ceee896da05bb49aa097cf351e1d5e`. The original 84 one-key neutral exchanges and 51 endpoints are those of EC49FNV; the preceding *auxiliary-state* forcing-core census is EC49FOE ([PR #2374](https://github.com/awdawmip/enterprise-math/pull/2374)). This study addresses an additional question: **does high-order blocking occur at an actual visited solver node?**

## Exact mathematical statement

The frozen native model has 94 cache keys, 178,850 lawful ordered signed-prefix words, 24 numbered demands and roots 03,05,06,07. Rooted signed-prefix minimum cover `D_{K,r}(S)` is the exact minimal number of trie prefix nodes covering all required labels in S (additional covered labels allowed). For a lawful partial root assignment `p=(S_03,S_05,S_06,S_07)`, write `LB_K(p)=sum_r D_{K,r}(S_r)` and, for a subset T of the unassigned labels U,

`f_{K,p}(T)=min_{legal allocations rho of T} sum_r D_{K,r}(S_r union T_r(rho))`.

The exact original cutoff is B=155. The native deterministic solver orders demand labels by (eligible-root count ascending, best singleton cost descending, label ascending); at each level root choices are considered in root order 03,05,06,07. An actual DFS node is a lawful assignment of the first d labels in this order that was not cut by an earlier lower-bound test.

**Lemma (maximal-cardinality blocking certificate).** Because each rooted cover cost D is monotone in its required labels, the completion value f is monotone under T subset T'. If `f(U)>B` and `f(U minus {i})<=B` for every i in U, then **U is the unique inclusion-minimal strictly blocking set and its least blocking cardinality is exactly |U|**. Every proper subset is contained in an (|U|-1)-set, so this follows directly from monotonicity. Only |U|+1 exact completion optimizations are needed for this certificate. If the assigned labels form an actual DFS prefix and `LB(p)<=B`, monotonicity of LB along the path verifies that all earlier prefixes survived.

## New finite exact census

On every one of the **51 distinct endpoint configurations** of the original **84 neutral one-key exchanges**, reconstruct all four native root cost tables from frozen signed-prefix words and traverse the *actual* DFS at B=155. At each visited, not-yet-cut nonterminal node p, compute the full completion f(U); for those with f(U)>155, compute all one-demand deletions. Let M(K) be the **largest** size |U| among actual visited nodes satisfying the above maximal-cardinality certificate.

| M(K) | Configuration count | Distinguishing configurations |
| ---: | ---: | --- |
| 2 | 4 | 32275, 32288, 32689, 32703 |
| 4 | 3 | 32276, 32290, 32304 |
| 5 | 43 | Includes 32315, 32318, 32296 |
| **7** | **1** | **32279** |

All 51 M(K) are positive. The actual DFS visits **436** nodes for K=32279 and **173** nodes for each of its actual one-key neighbors 32315 and 32318, while the full 24-demand optimum/counter/next-cost triple remains `(154,1,155)`. Of the 84 undirected original neutral edges, exactly **two** have unequal endpoint M, namely `32315↔32279` and `32318↔32279`; exactly **six** have unequal actual DFS visit counts. A node visit includes recursion entries at cut nodes and complete leaves; it is an operation count, not a benchmarked speedup.

The p=(0,5,138,8192) state of EC49FOC–FOE, with its auxiliary 18-label obstruction, does not lie on the deterministic DFS prefix path. This study locates high-order obstruction in the actual visited solver instead.

## Independently certified real DFS witnesses

| K | Actual depth | Partial native 24-bit root masks in order 03/05/06/07 | Future labels in DFS order | LB | max cost over size-(n−1) sets | f(U) | Exact h* |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **32279** | 17 | `(2048,5312837,8668698,0)` | `(5,7,15,17,19,21,13)` | 120 | 154 | 156 | **7** |
| **32315** | 19 | `(0,5312869,8668698,10240)` | `(7,15,17,19,21)` | 141 | 155 | 156 | **5** |

The complete exact horizon maxima H_0..H_n are:

- 32279: `(120,130,138,144,147,151,154,156)`.
- 32315: `(141,145,149,152,155,156)`.

An independent Python verifier reconstructs rooted signed-prefix tries directly from the frozen words, checks every prefix label against the native sorting rule and every prefix lower bound against 155, then enumerates **all 128** and **all 32** remaining-demand subsets, respectively. In both cases only the entire future set is strictly blocking. These are **two distinct reachable nodes**, since the root domains and solver label priority depend on K; no common-state invariance is assumed.

## Verification and limits

The author-side C++17 implementation reproduces the original trie/subset-DP kernel and the original cutoff-DFS semantics. Complete 51-row output includes every visit count and depth-wise counts of doomed prefixes and full-future minimal cores. The results and witness logs matched byte-for-byte when compiled at `-O2` and `-O3`. Python separately checked the two highlighted witnesses, not the entire 51-row census. The finite sample is precisely the 84 original neutral edges; no claim is made about all 38,169 recorded caches, physical X6 dynamics, or wall-clock algorithmic improvement.

For reproduction, compile `VERIFY_EC49FOF_DFS.cpp` with C++17 and run it with `FIRST_NEUTRAL_EDGES_EC49FNS.txt` as the sole argument and the frozen `master_and_radius3_cases.txt` on stdin. Run `VERIFY_EC49FOF_WITNESS.py master_and_radius3_cases.txt WITNESS_CERT.json` alongside `VERIFY_EC49FNY_INDEPENDENT.py`, already preserved in EC49FOD/EC49FOE provenance. Complete executable sources, the 51-row census, the witness certificates and hashes are in the companion evidence archive.

## Next discriminating question

Decompose the observed 436-versus-173 node difference into lawful-root eligibility, changed root cover cost and the deterministic label-order effect; determine whether a small disturbance certificate predicts changes in real-node M(K) without repeating the entire DFS. Benchmark any proposed lookahead method with its complete preprocessing and checking costs.

This is a standalone scientific-source preservation for an unpublished topic; no formal CLAIM/Result, independent mathematical review, or P000/worldview change is asserted.
